narr: Heavy rain and resultant flash flooding occurred during the afternoon hours. The rain was caused by a combination of a slow moving cold front along with moisture in connection with Tropical Storm Eta, which eventually would track across the northeastern Gulf of Mexico, across northern Florida, and well off of the NC coast. While rain began the day before, on November 10th, the heaviest of the rain fell through the afternoon hours of November 11th. Storm total rainfall amounts of 3 to 6 were common across much of Eastern NC, with 6 to 8 falling near areas such as Snow Hill, Kinston and northern Duplin County. Numerous reports of flash flooding occurred around the area. In addition to the heavy rain, in the heavier showers it was quite breezy with winds of 35 to 45 MPH quite common. In exposed areas near or over the water the wind was stronger, with many places gusting over 50 mph.
ev: Numerous roads were flooded in and around Jacksonville. Some roads that were flooded were Huff Dr, Pony Farm Rd, Vandergrift Dr, Maplehurst Rd, and Walnut Dr.
Several roads were flooded in and around Faison. Numerous fields around town were submerged. Nearby Highways 403 and 50 were flooded.
Water was reported to have been covering the roads in numerous locations around the county. The intersection of Carey and Hillandale Rd was closed due to high water.
Water-covered roads were reported around the county. Some locations that were flooded were Old New Bern Rd, 10-Mile Ford Rd, and Greentown Rd. The time was estimated based on radar data.
Various roads were flooded in and around Greenville. Rural two lane roads across the county were also flooded, as well as one water covered bridge.
